+# sdpa_fp8
+
+Build a regular FP8 scaled dot-product attention operation in a cuDNN frontend
+PyGraph.
+
+## Python synopsis
+
+```python
+o, stats, amax_s, amax_o = graph.sdpa_fp8(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    descale_q,
+    descale_k,
+    descale_v,
+    descale_s,
+    scale_s,
+    scale_o,
+    *,
+    attn_scale=None,
+    bias=None,
+    use_alibi_mask=False,
+    use_padding_mask=False,
+    seq_len_q=None,
+    seq_len_kv=None,
+    dropout=None,
+    rng_dump=None,
+    paged_attention_k_table=None,
+    paged_attention_v_table=None,
+    paged_attention_max_seq_len_kv=None,
+    compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.NOT_SET,
+    name="",
+    fn=None,
+    generate_stats=None,
+    score_max=None,
+    score_sum_exp=None,
+    sink_token=None,
+    diagonal_alignment=cudnn.diagonal_alignment.TOP_LEFT,
+    left_bound=None,
+    right_bound=None,
+    sliding_window=None,
+    use_causal_mask=False,
+    use_causal_mask_bottom_right=False,
+    is_inference=None,
+)
+```
+
+`sdpa_fp8` computes the SDPA forward pass with FP8 Q, K, V, and output scaling:
+
+```text
+q_d = descale_q * q
+k_d = descale_k * k
+v_d = descale_v * v
+scores = matmul(q_d, transpose(k_d))
+scores = scores * attn_scale              # only when attn_scale is provided
+scores = fn(scores)                       # optional score modifier function
+scores = scores + bias                    # optional
+scores = scores + alibi / diagonal mask   # optional additive term
+scores = scores + padding mask            # optional additive term
+stats = logsumexp(scores)                 # only when generate_stats=True
+probs = softmax(scores)
+probs = dropout(probs)                    # optional; applied after softmax
+o_unscaled = matmul(probs, v_d)
+amax_s = max(abs(scores))
+amax_o = max(abs(o_unscaled))
+o = quantize_fp8(o_unscaled, scale_o)
+```
+
+Equivalently, with dequantized inputs $\bar{Q}$, $\bar{K}$, and $\bar{V}$,
+optional score modifier function $f$, additive bias $B$, optional additive
+mask terms $M_d$ and $M_p$, and quantization function $Q_{\mathrm{fp8}}$:
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\bar{Q} &= d_q Q,\quad \bar{K} = d_k K,\quad \bar{V} = d_v V, \\
+S &= \bar{Q}\bar{K}^{\top}, \\
+\hat{S} &= f\left(\alpha S\right) + B + M_d + M_p, \\
+\operatorname{Stats} &= \operatorname{logsumexp}\left(\hat{S}\right), \\
+P &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\hat{S}\right), \\
+\tilde{P} &= \operatorname{dropout}\left(P\right), \\
+\bar{O} &= \tilde{P}\bar{V}, \\
+\operatorname{Amax}_S &= \max\left|\hat{S}\right|,\quad
+\operatorname{Amax}_O = \max\left|\bar{O}\right|, \\
+O &= Q_{\mathrm{fp8}}\left(s_o \bar{O}\right).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Here $d_q$, $d_k$, $d_v$, and $s_o$ correspond to `descale_q`,
+`descale_k`, `descale_v`, and `scale_o`. The `scale_s` and `descale_s`
+tensors control the backend's FP8 score-intermediate scaling; the equation shows
+the logical score tensor $\hat{S}$ and its reported $\operatorname{Amax}_S$.
+Terms for disabled options are omitted. When dropout is disabled,
+$\tilde{P} = P$.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `q` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): FP8 query tensor. Usually shape
+  `(B, H_q, S_q, D_qk)` with head-dimension stride `1`. Repository FP8 samples
+  use `cudnn.data_type.FP8_E4M3` through graph IO dtype or explicit tensor dtype.
+
+- `k` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): FP8 key tensor. Usually shape
+  `(B, H_k, S_kv, D_qk)`. With paged attention, this is the key-cache container
+  and `paged_attention_k_table` supplies logical page lookup.
+
+- `v` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): FP8 value tensor. Usually shape
+  `(B, H_v, S_kv, D_v)`. With paged attention, this is the value-cache
+  container and `paged_attention_v_table` supplies logical page lookup.
+
+- `descale_q`, `descale_k`, `descale_v` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Scalar-like
+  `FLOAT` descale tensors for Q, K, and V. Repository examples use shape
+  `(1, 1, 1, 1)` and stride `(1, 1, 1, 1)`.
+
+- `descale_s` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Scalar-like `FLOAT` descale tensor for
+  the FP8 score intermediate.
+
+- `scale_s` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Scalar-like `FLOAT` scale tensor for the
+  FP8 score intermediate.
+
+- `scale_o` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Scalar-like `FLOAT` scale tensor for
+  output quantization.
+
+- `attn_scale` (`float`, `cudnn.tensor`, or `None`, default `None`): Optional
+  scale multiplied into the attention scores after `Q @ K.T`. Pass
+  `1 / sqrt(D_qk)` explicitly when that is desired.
+
+- `bias` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`): Optional additive score

+
+- `use_alibi_mask` (`bool`, default `False`): Enables ALiBi score offsets where

+
+- `use_padding_mask` (`bool`, default `False`): Enables variable-length masking.

+
+- `seq_len_q`, `seq_len_kv` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`): Actual

+
+- `rng_dump` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`): Optional RNG-mask dump

+  `(B, H_q, S_q, S_kv)` or `(B, H_q, S_q, paged_attention_max_seq_len_kv)` for
+  paged attention, contiguous score stride ending in `1`, and `FLOAT` dtype.
+
+- `paged_attention_k_table`, `paged_attention_v_table` (`cudnn.tensor` or
+  `None`, default `None`): Optional `INT32` page tables. Entries are block
+  indices into the key or value cache container.
+
+- `paged_attention_max_seq_len_kv` (`int` or `None`, default `None`): Logical
+  maximum KV sequence length for paged attention. Do not specify it unless at
+  least one page table is provided.
+
+- `compute_data_type` (`cudnn.data_type`, default `NOT_SET`): Compute type. FP8
+  samples use `FLOAT`.
+
+- `name` (`str`, default `""`): Operation name.
+
+- `fn` (callable or `None`, default `None`): Optional score modifier function
+  `fn(sdpa_graph, score_tensor) -> cudnn.tensor`.
+
+- `generate_stats` (`bool` or `None`, default `None`): Whether to return softmax
+  statistics for backward. Exactly one of `generate_stats` and deprecated
+  `is_inference` must be specified.
+
+- `score_max`, `score_sum_exp` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`):

+

+  bias. Shape is `(1, H_q, 1, 1)` and dtype is `FLOAT`.
+
+- `diagonal_alignment` (`cudnn.diagonal_alignment`, default `TOP_LEFT`):
+  Alignment for diagonal band masks.
+
+- `left_bound`, `right_bound` (`int` or `None`, default `None`): Preferred

+
+Deprecated parameters:
+
+- `sliding_window` (`int` or `None`, default `None`): Deprecated left-window
+  shortcut. Prefer `left_bound`.
+
+- `use_causal_mask` (`bool`, default `False`): Deprecated causal shortcut.
+  Prefer `right_bound=0` with the desired `diagonal_alignment`.
+

+## Returns

+# sdpa_mxfp8
+
+Build an MXFP8 scaled dot-product attention operation in a cuDNN frontend
+PyGraph.
+
+## Python synopsis
+
+```python
+o, stats, amax_o = graph.sdpa_mxfp8(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    descale_q,
+    descale_k,
+    descale_v,
+    *,
+    attn_scale=None,
+    diagonal_alignment=cudnn.diagonal_alignment.TOP_LEFT,
+    diagonal_band_left_bound=None,
+    diagonal_band_right_bound=None,
+    compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.NOT_SET,
+    name="",
+    generate_stats,
+    sink_token=None,
+    unfuse_fma=False,
+    use_causal_mask=False,
+    use_causal_mask_bottom_right=False,
+)
+```
+
+`sdpa_mxfp8` computes SDPA with FP8 data tensors and block-wise MXFP8 scale
+factors:
+
+```text
+q_d = block_dequantize(q, descale_q)
+k_d = block_dequantize(k, descale_k)
+v_d = block_dequantize(v, descale_v)
+scores = matmul(q_d, transpose(k_d))
+scores = scores * attn_scale              # only when attn_scale is provided
+scores = scores + diagonal / causal mask  # optional additive term
+stats = logsumexp(scores)                 # only when generate_stats=True
+probs = softmax(scores)
+o_unscaled = matmul(probs, v_d)
+amax_o = max(abs(o_unscaled))
+o = output_cast(o_unscaled)
+```
+
+Equivalently, with block-dequantized inputs $\bar{Q}$, $\bar{K}$, and
+$\bar{V}$, optional additive diagonal mask term $M_d$, and output cast function
+$C$:
+
+$$
+\begin{aligned}
+\bar{Q} &= \operatorname{block\_dequant}(Q, S_Q), \\
+\bar{K} &= \operatorname{block\_dequant}(K, S_K), \\
+\bar{V} &= \operatorname{block\_dequant}(V, S_V), \\
+S &= \bar{Q}\bar{K}^{\top}, \\
+\hat{S} &= \alpha S + M_d, \\
+\operatorname{Stats} &= \operatorname{logsumexp}\left(\hat{S}\right), \\
+P &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\hat{S}\right), \\
+\bar{O} &= P\bar{V}, \\
+\operatorname{Amax}_O &= \max\left|\bar{O}\right|, \\
+O &= C\left(\bar{O}\right).
+\end{aligned}
+$$
+
+Here $S_Q$, $S_K$, and $S_V$ correspond to `descale_q`, `descale_k`, and
+`descale_v`. The factor $\alpha$ is `attn_scale` when provided; otherwise the
+multiplication by $\alpha$ is omitted. Terms for disabled masks are omitted.
+`sdpa_mxfp8` does not expose the regular FP8 score modifier function, dropout,
+bias, padding mask, or paged-attention parameters.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `q` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Query tensor with dtype
+  `cudnn.data_type.FP8_E4M3`. Shape is `(B, H, S_q, D)`. The head-dimension
+  stride should be `1` for the supported layouts.
+
+- `k` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Key tensor with dtype
+  `cudnn.data_type.FP8_E4M3`. Shape is `(B, H, S_kv, D)`.
+
+- `v` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): Value tensor with dtype
+  `cudnn.data_type.FP8_E4M3`. Shape is `(B, H, S_kv, D)` in the documented
+  MXFP8 forward signature.
+
+- `descale_q` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): MXFP8 block scale-factor tensor for
+  Q. Must use dtype `cudnn.data_type.FP8_E8M0` and
+  `reordering_type=cudnn.tensor_reordering.F8_128x4`. Shape is
+  `(B, H, S_q_padded, D_scale_padded)`, where `D_scale = ceil(D / 32)` and the
+  scale dimension is padded to a multiple of `4`. The last stride must be `1`.
+
+- `descale_k` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): MXFP8 block scale-factor tensor for
+  K. Same dtype, reordering, shape pattern, and last-stride requirement as
+  `descale_q`; `S_kv_padded` is padded to a multiple of `128`.
+
+- `descale_v` (`cudnn.tensor`, required): MXFP8 block scale-factor tensor for
+  V. Must use dtype `FP8_E8M0` and reordering `F8_128x4`. Shape is
+  `(B, H, S_scale_padded, D_padded)`, where `S_scale = ceil(S_kv / 32)` and the
+  scale dimension is padded to a multiple of `4`. The sequence-scale stride
+  `stride[2]` must be `1`.
+
+- `attn_scale` (`float`, `cudnn.tensor`, or `None`, default `None`): Optional
+  score scale applied after `Q @ K.T`.
+
+- `diagonal_alignment` (`cudnn.diagonal_alignment`, default `TOP_LEFT`):
+  Alignment used by diagonal band masks.
+
+- `diagonal_band_left_bound` (`int` or `None`, default `None`): Optional left
+  diagonal-band bound. Do not combine it with deprecated sliding-window
+  spellings; `sdpa_mxfp8` does not expose a non-deprecated `sliding_window`
+  parameter.
+
+- `diagonal_band_right_bound` (`int` or `None`, default `None`): Optional right
+  diagonal-band bound. Prefer `diagonal_band_right_bound=0` over deprecated
+  causal-mask shortcuts.
+
+- `compute_data_type` (`cudnn.data_type`, default `NOT_SET`): Compute type.
+  Examples construct the graph with `compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT`.
+
+- `name` (`str`, default `""`): Operation name.
+
+- `generate_stats` (`bool`, required): Whether to create the softmax
+  statistics tensor. Use `True` when a backward graph will consume `stats`.
+
+- `sink_token` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`): Optional sink token
+  bias. Shape is `(1, H, 1, 1)` and dtype is `FLOAT`.
+
+- `unfuse_fma` (`bool`, default `False`): SM100 softmax option that requests
+  unfused multiply and add instructions instead of fused FMA where supported.
+
+Deprecated masking parameters:
+
+- `use_causal_mask` (`bool`, default `False`): Deprecated causal-mask shortcut.
+  Prefer `diagonal_band_right_bound=0`.
+
+- `use_causal_mask_bottom_right` (`bool`, default `False`): Deprecated
+  bottom-right causal shortcut. Prefer
+  `diagonal_alignment=cudnn.diagonal_alignment.BOTTOM_RIGHT` with
+  `diagonal_band_right_bound=0`.
+
+## Returns
+
+- `o` (`cudnn.tensor`): Attention output tensor. The output dtype is configured
+  on the returned tensor; repository examples set it to `BFLOAT16`.
+
+- `stats` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`): Softmax statistics when
+  `generate_stats=True`; otherwise `None`.
+
+- `amax_o` (`cudnn.tensor`): Absolute maximum of the output tensor, normally
+  shape `(1, 1, 1, 1)`, stride `(1, 1, 1, 1)`, and dtype `FLOAT`.
+
+## Raises
+
+- `TypeError`: Raised immediately for invalid tensor arguments, missing required
+  `generate_stats`, invalid enum values, or malformed scalar values.
+
+- `RuntimeError`: Raised immediately for conflicting deprecated and preferred
+  mask options detected by the binding.
+
+- `ValueError`: Raised by `graph.validate()` for malformed MXFP8 scale-factor
+  metadata, wrong reordering, wrong dtype, invalid output metadata, or
+  inconsistent diagonal-mask options.
+
+- `cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError`: Raised by `graph.check_support()` or
+  `graph.build_plans()` when MXFP8 SDPA is unsupported by the installed cuDNN
+  version, GPU architecture, dtype, stride, or feature combination.
+

+# tensor
+
+Create a graph tensor attribute from explicit shape, stride, dtype, and tensor metadata.
+
+## Python synopsis
+
+```python
+X = graph.tensor(
+    dim,
+    stride,
+    data_type=cudnn.data_type.NOT_SET,
+    is_virtual=False,
+    is_pass_by_value=False,
+    ragged_offset=None,
+    reordering_type=cudnn.tensor_reordering.NONE,
+    name="",
+    uid=-1,
+)
+```
+
+`graph.tensor(...)` creates a `cudnn.tensor` graph attribute only. It does not allocate device memory. Non-virtual inputs and outputs receive their runtime buffers later through the variant pack passed to `graph.execute(...)` or `graph.execute_plan_at_index(...)`.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `dim` (`Sequence[int]`, required): Logical tensor dimensions. The number of values is the tensor rank. Use positive dimension values for static shapes. Graphs created with dynamic-shape or override-shape support may accept compatible runtime shapes through lifecycle APIs that take `override_shapes`.
+
+- `stride` (`Sequence[int]`, required): Logical strides in elements, not bytes. `stride` must have the same length as `dim`. Related tensors do not need to have the same stride unless an operation-specific page says so.
+
+- `data_type` (`cudnn.data_type`, default `cudnn.data_type.NOT_SET`): Tensor element type. If left as `NOT_SET`, operation or graph defaults may fill it later, but user-visible inputs and outputs are clearer when the type is set explicitly.
+
+- `is_virtual` (`bool`, default `False`): Marks the tensor as an internal graph intermediate that does not require a user-provided runtime buffer. A materialized graph output should normally be non-virtual and marked with `set_output(True)`.
+
+- `is_pass_by_value` (`bool`, default `False`): Marks a scalar or small parameter as passed by value through the variant pack. This is used for runtime scalar inputs such as normalization epsilon, attention scale, dropout seed, or dropout offset.
+
+- `ragged_offset` (`cudnn.tensor` or `None`, default `None`): Optional tensor describing packed ragged storage offsets. It is consumed by APIs that support ragged or THD layouts. The offset tensor must satisfy the dtype, shape, and stride requirements of the consuming operation.
+
+- `reordering_type` (`cudnn.tensor_reordering`, default `cudnn.tensor_reordering.NONE`): Optional special memory-reordering metadata. MXFP8 scale-factor tensors commonly use `cudnn.tensor_reordering.F8_128x4`.
+
+- `name` (`str`, default `""`): User-visible tensor name. Names are useful for debugging, generated output names, serialization, and readable error messages.
+
+- `uid` (`int`, default `-1`): Optional explicit frontend UID. Leave this as `-1` for normal graph construction. Explicit UIDs are mainly useful for serialized graphs, external descriptors, tests, or variant packs keyed by UID.
+
+## Returns
+
+- `X` (`cudnn.tensor`): A Python binding of C++ `Tensor_attributes`. The returned object can be passed to graph operations and further configured with methods such as `set_output(True)`, `set_data_type(...)`, `set_dim(...)`, and `set_stride(...)`.
+
+## Raises
+
+- `TypeError`: Raised immediately when `dim`, `stride`, enums, booleans, `ragged_offset`, `name`, or `uid` cannot be converted to the bound C++ types.
+
+- `ValueError`: Raised later by `graph.validate()` for malformed tensor metadata, missing required attributes, invalid names, duplicate explicit UIDs, or shape-deduction failures in consuming operations.
+
+- `cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError`: Raised by support checking or plan building when the tensor dtype, layout, dimensions, or consuming operation are unsupported by the selected backend path.
+
+- `RuntimeError`: Raised by later lifecycle methods for CUDA, cuDNN backend, handle, invalid value, or execution failures.

+# tensor_like
+
+Create a graph tensor by cloning existing tensor metadata or by importing metadata from a DLPack object.
+
+## Python synopsis
+
+```python
+Y = graph.tensor_like(input, name="")
+Z = graph.tensor_like(dlpack_object)
+```
+
+The first overload copies metadata from another `cudnn.tensor`. The second overload creates a graph tensor from an object that exposes `__dlpack__`, such as a PyTorch tensor.
+
+## Parameters
+
+- `input` (`cudnn.tensor`, required for the first overload): Existing graph tensor attributes to copy. The copy keeps shape, stride, dtype, virtual state, pass-by-value state, ragged-offset metadata, and reordering metadata, but receives a fresh frontend UID and the supplied `name`.
+
+- `name` (`str`, default `""`): Name assigned to the cloned tensor for the `tensor_like(input, name)` overload. Names are not copied from `input`.
+
+- `dlpack_object` (object with `__dlpack__`, required for the second overload): Runtime object whose DLPack capsule supplies shape, stride, dtype, and device metadata. If the DLPack strides pointer is `NULL`, the binding treats the object as compact row-major and generates row-major strides. CPU DLPack tensors are marked pass-by-value; CUDA and CUDA-managed tensors are regular runtime-buffer tensors.

+## Returns

+- `Y` or `Z` (`cudnn.tensor`): A graph tensor attribute registered as a graph input. A tensor imported from DLPack is non-virtual and infers dtype, dimensions, and strides from the capsule.

+
+- `TypeError`: Raised immediately when the arguments do not match either overload or when `name` cannot be converted to `str`.

+- `ValueError`: Raised when the DLPack object does not expose `__dlpack__`, the capsule is invalid, the DLPack device type is not CPU, CUDA host, CUDA device, or CUDA managed memory, or later validation finds malformed tensor metadata.

+- `cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError`: Raised by later support checking or plan building when the imported dtype, shape, stride, or consuming operation is unsupported.

+# API layers and graph lifecycle
+
+cuDNN Frontend has several user-facing layers that share operations but own different amounts of lifecycle and integration behavior.
+
+## API layers
+
+`cudnn.Graph` is a PyTorch-oriented wrapper. It owns a `cudnn.pygraph`, runs lifecycle stages at context exit, allocates workspace and outputs, and makes the built graph callable.
+
+`cudnn.pygraph` is the explicit Python IR. It owns tensor and node objects, validates and freezes them, ranks manifest-discovered Python engines with cuDNN backend plans, and binds caller resources at execution.
+
+`cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph` is the modern header-only C++ API. It exposes graph attributes, operation construction, planning, filters, serialization, CUDA Graph integration, and explicit execution resources.
+
+Decorators in `cudnn.graph` build and cache `cudnn.Graph` instances. `cudnn.ops` and `cudnn.experimental.ops` register PyTorch operators. Optional OSS packages call architecture-specific CUTLASS DSL kernels directly or participate through engine selection.
+
+The legacy C++ builder API constructs backend descriptors individually. It remains a compatibility surface, not the preferred learning path.
+
+## Graph lifecycle
+
+| Stage | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Describe the IR | Tensors, operations, attributes, and output intent are explicit. |
+| Validate | Graph invariants and inferred metadata are checked. |
+| Create the graph representation | User attributes become cuDNN backend operation descriptors. |
+| Create and rank plans | Heuristics discover engine configurations, including modes A, B, and fallback where requested. |
+| Check and build | Unsupported candidates are rejected and reusable executable plans are compiled. |
+| Bind and execute | Runtime data and workspace are bound without changing graph structure. |
+
+The graph freezes when creating the graph representation or planning needs stable identity. Create a new graph for incompatible metadata or policy; do not mutate tensor UIDs, names, shapes, or node attributes behind a built plan.
+
+See [Python IR routing invariants](/concepts/python-ir-routing) for UID ownership, plan index spaces, engine decline semantics, freeze boundaries, output layout ownership, and dispatch testing.
+
+Python IR routing and pure-Python engines are unreleased in this checkout; the
+[routing page](/concepts/python-ir-routing#availability) records their current
+availability.

+# Attention support history and benchmarks
+
+Use this page to understand when major SDPA capabilities entered cuDNN and where repository benchmark artifacts are produced. For deployment decisions, the individual SDPA API page and `check_support()` on the installed backend remain authoritative.
+
+## Historical feature milestones
+
+| cuDNN | SDPA milestone recorded by the repository's former guide |
+| --- | --- |
+| 8.9.3 | Initial FP16/BF16 SDPA on SM80+ |
+| 8.9.6 | Padding, ALiBi, and bias masks |
+| 9.0 | Sequence lengths no longer required to be multiples of 64 |
+| 9.1 | FP8 SDPA on Hopper and newer |
+| 9.2 | Sliding-window attention |
+| 9.3 | Bottom-right causal masking for FP16/BF16 |
+| 9.5 | Paged attention and dBias with variable sequence lengths |
+| 9.6 | GQA with ragged offsets and broader bottom-right causal lengths |
+| 9.7 | FP8 bottom-right causal masking on SM100+ and paged plus ragged composition |
+| 9.9 | Broader decode head dimensions |
+| 9.10.2 | Packed page tables; 9.10.0 and 9.10.1 were historically marked problematic |
+| 9.11 | DeepSeek asymmetric head dimensions in selected Hopper/Blackwell backward paths |
+| 9.13 | Unified SDPA, FP8-to-FP16/BF16 output on Blackwell, and sink tokens |
+| 9.14 | Unified block masks; the former guide recorded a noncausal sliding-window issue for large KV sequences |
+| 9.15 | Unified padding masks and paged inputs |
+| 9.18 | Ragged support on Ampere/Ada and deterministic FP16/BF16 on Blackwell |
+| 9.19 | Deterministic FP8 on Blackwell and FP8 QK=192/V=128 |
+| 9.21 | Unified SM100 `unfuse_fma` control |
+
+This table is historical context, not a complete compatibility matrix. Minor releases can contain fixes, and one feature's first appearance does not imply compatibility with every mask, layout, dtype, backward mode, or architecture.
+
+## Flex attention controls
+
+Current SDPA forward accepts `score_mod`, which builds a pointwise subgraph over the score tensor. Backward accepts the forward modifier and a corresponding `score_mod_bprop` callback. Inputs used by the modifier must first be registered in the parent graph, then passed into the callback's subgraph.
+
+Custom score modifiers are not freely composable with every built-in ALiBi, padding, causal, sliding-window, or block-mask implementation. The current support checks reject unsupported combinations. Block masks use the implementation's packed tile representation; do not assume a framework boolean mask can be passed directly.
+
+## Logical and physical layouts
+
+BHSD and BSHD describe logical axis orders. The frontend ultimately uses explicit dimensions and strides, so two tensors with the same logical labels can have different physical storage. Dense SDPA samples commonly use BSHD or BHSD dimensions and encode physical storage through strides. BMHK is equivalent historical notation for BSHD and appears only where an interface or older source uses those letters.
+
+When converting from a framework tensor, preserve its actual stride. Do not relabel a view as another layout unless the stride describes that storage and the selected backend supports it.
+
+## Determinism
+
+Forward SDPA is deterministic for a fixed supported plan and inputs unless the chosen feature introduces stochastic state such as dropout. Backward determinism is architecture, dtype, feature, and version dependent. Request `use_deterministic_algorithm=True`, then require `check_support()` to succeed; do not infer determinism from architecture alone.
+
+## Repository benchmark suites
+
+The current benchmark runner covers Llama 3.1, DeepSeek V3, Kimi-K2.6, GPT-OSS, Qwen 3.5, Wan 2.2, LTX-2, and autoregressive video-DiT configurations. It can compare cuDNN with available FlashAttention backends for BF16, FP8, and MXFP8 paths, with forward, backward, mask, and determinism controls.
+
+The checked-in GB200 and GB300 result directories include CSV data and generated charts. The former guide highlighted these representative cases:
+
+| Workload | Q heads | KV heads | Head dimensions | Masks |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
+| Llama 3.1 | 64 | 8 | QK=V=128 | top-left causal and no mask |
+| DeepSeek V3 | 128 | 128 | QK=192, V/O=128 | top-left causal and no mask |

+See the [benchmark instructions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/0a07d4ee28f8ae2f2106bb766b1878cc732ee80c/benchmark/sdpa_benchmark_training/README.md) and [checked-in result artifacts](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/0a07d4ee28f8ae2f2106bb766b1878cc732ee80c/benchmark/sdpa_benchmark_training/results). +# Attention layouts, masks, and state
+
+SDPA computes scores from query and key, modifies and masks those scores, applies softmax and optional dropout, then multiplies by value.
+
+## Tensor layouts
+
+The layout letters name the tensor axes and the order in which they appear:
+
+| Layout | Shape | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| BSHD / BMHK | `[B, S, H, D]` / `[B, M, H, K]` | `B` is batch size, `S` or `M` is sequence length, `H` is the number of heads, and `D` or `K` is the embedding dimension per head. BSHD is the name used most often in this project; BMHK is equivalent notation with different letters for the same axes. |
+| BHSD | `[B, H, S, D]` | `B` is batch size, `H` is the number of heads, `S` is sequence length, and `D` is the embedding dimension per head. Compared with BSHD, the head axis appears before the sequence axis. |
+| THD | `[T, H, D]` | `T` is the total number of valid tokens across the batch, `H` is the number of heads, and `D` is the embedding dimension per head. Tokens from variable-length sequences are packed together without padding, and cumulative sequence lengths or ragged offsets identify each sequence. For sequence lengths $S_i$, $T = \sum_i S_i$. |
+
+These names describe an axis convention, but explicit dimensions and strides remain authoritative. Two tensors with the same logical axes can use different physical storage when their strides differ.
+
+[GQA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_%28deep_learning%29#Multi-Query_Attention) (grouped-query attention) uses more query heads than key/value heads. Each key/value head is shared by a group of query heads; for example, 32 query heads and 8 key/value heads form groups of four query heads. Q, K, and V can use the same axis convention and compatible physical layouts; the defining difference is that Q has more heads than K and V. The query-head count must be divisible by the key/value-head count for equal-sized groups.
+
+## Masks
+
+Diagonal bands express causal and sliding windows. Alignment determines whether the diagonal is top-left or bottom-right. Padding masks use per-batch sequence lengths. Block masks pack tile visibility. Score modifier functions insert custom score dataflow and can conflict with built-in mask implementations.
+
+## Statistics and dropout
+
+Training forward can emit log-sum-exp statistics for backward. Dropout applies after softmax and uses either Philox seed/offset state or an explicit mask and scale. RNG state must advance according to the application's reproducibility policy.
+
+## KV caches
+
+Paged attention stores K/V in block containers and uses page tables of integer block indices. A logical maximum KV length controls score and RNG shapes. Sink tokens and cache updates are persistent application state, not virtual intermediates.
+
+## Precision
+
+FP8 and MXFP8 attention add input/output scales, descales, amax values, layout reorders, dimension limits, and architecture gates. Their contracts are not aliases for BF16 SDPA.
+
+For release milestones, logical-versus-physical layout guidance, determinism, Flex Attention controls, and benchmark provenance, see [Attention support history and benchmarks](/concepts/attention-support-history).

+# Compilation, reuse, caching, and deployment
+
+Reuse is valid only while graph structure, metadata, plan policy, and target compatibility remain within the built support surface.
+
+## Static graph reuse
+
+A static graph can execute repeatedly with new pointers when dimensions, strides, data types, operation attributes, and plan assumptions remain compatible. Wrapper and decorator caches turn those metadata values into keys.
+
+## Dynamic graphs
+
+Dynamic-shape and override-shape modes allow specific runtime metadata changes. The engine still defines a bounded support surface. Kernel caches store specializations; they do not make arbitrary shapes legal.
+
+## Serialization
+
+Backend serialization preserves a cuDNN graph representation, not arbitrary Python engines or inspection dictionaries. Device properties, target SM, backend version, and serialization compatibility determine whether another process or system can load it.
+
+## Warmup and AOT
+
+Warmup materializes lazy work before service. Deviceless AOT supplies target properties explicitly so compilation does not inspect a local GPU. Both require a fallback or rebuild policy when deployment compatibility changes.
+
+## Cache identity
+
+Include frontend and backend versions, CUDA/driver where relevant, GPU architecture, graph key, tensor metadata, operation attributes, engine/knob policy, and dynamic bounds. Reject partial matches rather than executing a stale plan.

+# Engines, heuristics, plans, routing, and autotuning
+
+An engine is an implementation family. A configuration chooses its knobs. An execution plan is a graph-specific built configuration. Heuristics propose candidates; filters apply application policy; autotuning measures eligible plans.
+
+## Python routing
+
+`cudnn.pygraph` discovers eligible Python engines from the library's static manifest. Family heuristics return ranked `PlanConfig(engine_id, knobs)` entries and place the cuDNN backend's heuristic block among them. There is no runtime engine-registration or router-replacement API.
+
+Backend entries retain their own backend-plan indices when those candidates are exposed; a delegating backend entry represents candidates that remain internal. The combined `graph.plans` index must never be passed directly as a backend index.
+
+This routed Python plan model is unreleased. See
+[Python IR routing availability](/concepts/python-ir-routing#availability) before
+depending on its representation or index-space contract.
+
+## C++ planning
+
+The C++ Graph API builds an operation graph, queries heuristic modes, filters engines or configurations, checks support, builds one or more plans, and executes a selected plan. Engine IDs and knob choices are backend- and graph-specific.
+
+## Notes and policy
+
+Behavior and numerical notes describe properties such as determinism, down-conversion, or runtime compilation. Workspace and shared-memory filters enforce resource budgets. A policy filter is not an accuracy test; validate representative outputs independently.
+
+## Autotuning
+
+Warm up, time on the intended stream, synchronize at measurement boundaries, and include representative addresses and shapes. Cache a choice with frontend/backend/driver/GPU and graph metadata. Re-tune when a compatibility field changes.

+# Fusion patterns and support semantics
+
+Use this page to answer two different questions:
+
+1. **Which fusion-like patterns does this frontend name explicitly?** Use the inventories below.
+2. **Will one concrete graph run on one concrete system?** Build an execution plan with the graph's real tensor metadata. There is no static, universal list for this question.
+
+cuDNN Frontend does not enumerate every graph that a cuDNN backend can fuse. A Graph exposes fusion opportunities; the selected execution plan decides how to implement them. Support can change with the cuDNN version, GPU, tensor dimensions, strides, data types, alignment, workspace limit, and numerical requirements. Backend engines are therefore [discovered per graph at plan time](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/python/cudnn/engines/router.py#L27-L36).
+
+This page covers the public patterns in this checkout. Source links are pinned to a repository commit so that API claims remain auditable. A listed composite, matcher, direct kernel, or working example does **not** guarantee that an arbitrary configuration is supported or that execution uses one physical kernel.
+
+## Choose the relevant support category
+
+| Category | What is statically enumerable | Authoritative support test |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Runtime-discovered backend graph | Graph operations and their semantics, but not every supported composition | The complete graph successfully reaches `build_plans()` with the application's metadata and policy |
+| Graph OSS matcher | The subgraph shape recognized by `heur_mode.OPENSOURCE` | The matcher accepts the exact graph and an OSS plan successfully builds |
+| Frontend composite operation | The public operation and its primitive expansion | The expanded graph successfully builds a plan |
+| Direct or specialized kernel | Exported class or wrapper names and their fixed operation composition | The API's validator accepts the inputs and the specialization compiles |
+| Repository example | One tested composition and its recorded metadata | Evidence only for that example; re-run planning for other metadata or environments |
+
+Do not use a successful `validate()` call as a support test. It proves graph structure and tensor metadata are valid, not that an execution engine or compiled plan exists.

+## Graph OSS matcher inventory
+
+`OPENSOURCE` planning has two registered matcher slots in this checkout. Selecting only `OPENSOURCE` provides no general fallback when neither slot matches. Combining it with ordinary heuristic modes also queries cuDNN backend candidates.
+
+### RMSNorm followed by SiLU
+
+- Pattern: `rmsnorm(INFERENCE) -> swish(beta=1)`.
+- Python: `graph.rmsnorm(...)`, then `graph.swish(...)`.
+- C++: `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::rmsnorm(...)`, then `Graph::pointwise(..., PointwiseMode_t::SWISH_FWD)`.
+- Matcher contract: the nodes are adjacent and connected by the same tensor UID; X and scale are BF16; epsilon is required; X has rank 2 or greater. Output may be BF16, E4M3 FP8, or NVFP4 subject to architecture gates.
+- Details: [normalization guide](/optional-kernels/oss-normalization) and [matcher source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/graph_interface.h#L460-L599).
+
+### One SDPA node
+
+- Pattern: one composite or unified SDPA node. A user-authored `matmul -> softmax -> matmul` chain is not this matcher.
+- Python: `graph.sdpa(...)`.
+- C++: `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa(...)`.
+- Matcher contract: current NVRTC prefill lookup accepts head dimension 64 or 128 on SM90 or the SM100 family. Registration alone does not validate every data type or optional SDPA feature; successful plan creation is authoritative.
+- Details: [matcher source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/graph_interface.h#L350-L458), [SM90 lookup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/experimental/sm90_sdpa_prefill_engine.h#L45-L82), and [SM100 lookup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/experimental/sm100_sdpa_prefill_engine.h#L54-L91).
+
+These are the only OSS matcher slots registered by [`Graph::create_execution_plans()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/graph_interface.h#L2815-L2842).

+## Frontend composite operation inventory
+
+A composite operation expands fixed semantics into primitive Graph nodes. The backend can fuse some or all of those primitives, execute them separately, or reject the graph.
+
+### SDPA forward composites
+
+| Variant | Python identifier | C++ identifier | Expansion and key limits |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Standard SDPA | `graph.sdpa` | `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa` | `Q @ K^T`, optional scale, score modification, mask or bias, softmax, optional dropout, then `P @ V` |
+| FP8 SDPA | `graph.sdpa_fp8` | `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa_fp8` | Standard dataflow plus per-tensor dequantization, scaling, quantization, and amax operations |
+| MXFP8 SDPA | `graph.sdpa_mxfp8` | MXFP8 overload of `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa_fp8` | Standard dataflow plus block-scale dequantization, scaling, quantization, and amax operations |
+
+The composite forward path rejects `block_mask`, cumulative sequence-length inputs, and ragged-offset multipliers. Consult the [composite expansion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/scaled_dot_product_flash_attention.h#L604-L1073), [support checks](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/sdpa_support_surface.h#L389-L546), and [Python SDPA reference](/api/python/sdpa) before allocating tensors.
+
+### SDPA backward composites
+
+| Variant | Python identifier | C++ identifier | Expansion and key limits |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Standard SDPA backward | `graph.sdpa_backward` | `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa_backward` | Recomputes probabilities and dropout, then forms dV, dP/dS, dK, and dQ; GQA and optional dBias add reductions |
+| FP8 SDPA backward | `graph.sdpa_fp8_backward` | `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa_fp8_backward` | Backward attention plus per-tensor dequantization, scaling, quantization, and amax reductions |
+| MXFP8 SDPA backward | `graph.sdpa_mxfp8_backward` | MXFP8 overload of `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::sdpa_fp8_backward` | Backward attention plus block-scale dequantization, scaling, quantization, and amax reductions |
+
+Standard dense inputs are rank 4 and require unit embedding stride. Head dimensions, masks, ragged layouts, dropout, determinism, and dBias are architecture- and version-dependent. Regular FP8 backward starts at cuDNN 9.1 on Hopper. See the [standard backward expansion](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/scaled_dot_product_flash_attention.h#L1075-L2057), [FP8 backward source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/sdpa_fp8_bwd.h#L17-L1120), and the [Python backward reference](/api/python/sdpa-backward).

+### Internal softmax fallback
+
+- Expansion: max reduction, subtraction, exponentiation, sum reduction, and division; optional sink and statistics add branches.
+- Public API: internal to composites before cuDNN 9.21; there is no standalone Python Graph operation.
+- Output modes: statistics only, max plus sum-exp, or none of those outputs.
+- Source: [softmax composite](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/softmax.h#L86-L217).
+
+### Diagonal-band mask fallback
+
+- Expansion: generate row and column indices, adjust bounds, compare, then binary-select scores or negative infinity.
+- Python: exposed through SDPA mask attributes.
+- C++: `cudnn_frontend::graph::Graph::diagonal_band_mask`.
+- Limit: before cuDNN 9.21, the composite rejects cumulative sequence lengths.
+- Details: [C++ reference](/api/cpp/diagonal-band-mask) and [mask composite](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d3c03b5881cdaccc4c0e07dd9ab4c7c6bc105715/include/cudnn_frontend/node/diagonal_band_mask.h#L121-L273).

+## Verify support for a concrete Graph
+
+Build and test the graph with the application's actual metadata. For Python, the support probe after graph construction is:
+
+```python
+graph.validate()
+graph.build_operation_graph()
+graph.create_execution_plans(
+    [
+        cudnn.heur_mode.OPENSOURCE,
+        cudnn.heur_mode.A,
+        cudnn.heur_mode.FALLBACK,
+    ]
+)
+graph.check_support()
+graph.build_plans(cudnn.build_plan_policy.HEURISTICS_CHOICE)
+```
+
+Use `[cudnn.heur_mode.OPENSOURCE]` when the application requires an OSS matcher and must fail rather than fall back. Omit `OPENSOURCE` when only cuDNN backend plans should be considered. The equivalent C++ modes are `cudnn_frontend::HeurMode_t::OPENSOURCE`, `A`, and `FALLBACK`; check every returned `cudnn_frontend::error_t` before continuing.
+
+### Interpret lifecycle failures
+
+| Last successful stage | What has been established | What has not been established |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `validate()` | Graph structure and tensor metadata are valid | Engine support |
+| `build_operation_graph()` | Backend operation descriptors were created | A candidate or compiled plan exists |
+| `create_execution_plans()` | Candidate discovery completed | A candidate supports every graph detail |
+| `check_support()` | At least one candidate plan supports the graph | Kernel or plan compilation succeeds |
+| `build_plans()` | A plan compiled for this graph and environment | Numerical correctness or one-kernel execution |
+| `execute()` plus reference comparison | This input case meets the tested numerical tolerance | Other shapes, types, layouts, GPUs, or versions are supported |
+
+After `build_plans()`, allocate `graph.get_workspace_size()` bytes, execute representative inputs, and compare outputs and applicable gradients with an independent reference. Repeat plan creation and numerical verification whenever the cuDNN frontend or backend version, GPU, dimensions, strides, data types, alignment, workspace policy, or numerical policy changes.
+
+For custom Python routing, assert the selected engine ID. For the cuDNN backend path, verify that a plan builds for the complete graph. Do not infer a one-kernel fusion from successful execution: backend engine names and kernel grouping are not stable public contracts. See [routing verification guidance](/concepts/python-ir-routing#prove-the-selected-path) and the [explicit lifecycle guide](/how-to/explicit-lifecycle).

+# Glossary
+
+**Backend graph**: the cuDNN operation graph representation created from frontend tensor and operation attributes.
+
+**Block scaling**: quantization in which one scale applies to a fixed-size block of values rather than an entire tensor.
+
+**Compute data type**: precision used by an operation's computation, often FP32 even when I/O is FP16 or BF16.
+
+**Execution plan**: an engine and configuration selected for a validated graph.
+
+**Graph representation creation**: conversion from frontend tensor and operation attributes into the cuDNN backend operation graph.
+
+**Frontend workspace**: temporary storage owned by graph execution in addition to any backend plan workspace.
+
+**Intermediate data type**: default type for virtual tensors between operations.
+
+**I/O data type**: default type for non-virtual graph inputs and outputs.
+
+**Pass-by-value tensor**: a scalar embedded or supplied from host memory rather than a device allocation.
+
+**Ragged offset**: a tensor describing variable-length storage offsets, optionally scaled by an element multiplier.
+
+**Routed plan**: a top-level Python `PlanConfig` selecting an in-tree Python engine or a cuDNN backend candidate; its combined-list index is not a backend plan index.
+
+**Tensor UID**: stable integer used to match graph tensors to runtime pointers.
+
+**Variant pack**: the runtime mapping from tensor descriptors or UIDs to device buffers plus workspace.
+
+**Virtual tensor**: an internal graph value that does not require a caller-owned device buffer.

+# Graphs, tensors, virtual values, and fusion
+
+A frontend graph is a directed acyclic dataflow graph. Operation nodes consume tensor descriptors and produce new descriptors. Runtime storage remains separate from those descriptors until execution.
+
+## Tensor identity
+
+Dimensions describe logical extents; strides describe storage. Data type controls representation, while compute type controls operation arithmetic. Names support readable lookup and wrapper IO contracts. Numeric UIDs are the stable backend identity used by variant packs and serialization.
+
+Names and UIDs must be unique in a graph. A ragged-offset tensor adds variable-length storage metadata. A pass-by-value tensor represents a scalar supplied through the backend scalar contract. Compile-time constants become part of graph identity.
+
+## Virtual values
+
+Operation outputs are virtual by default. A virtual value can connect nodes without a caller-owned device allocation. `set_output(True)` makes it non-virtual so execution must bind storage. Inputs, final outputs, saved statistics crossing graph boundaries, and externally inspected intermediates need non-virtual storage.
+
+## Fusion
+
+Graph composition exposes a fusion opportunity, but the selected engine decides implementation. Shape, stride, type, alignment, backend version, architecture, workspace, and numerical policy all influence available plans. The contract is the graph result and documented resource behavior, not a guaranteed kernel count. See [Fusion patterns and support semantics](/concepts/fusion-patterns) for the patterns that the frontend and fixed OSS kernels own explicitly, plus examples of backend-discovered compositions.
+
+## Ownership
+
+Python IR owns `Tensor` and `Node` objects; C++ Graph uses shared tensor attributes. Callers own runtime buffers, handles unless wrapped, and explicit workspace. Keep all resources alive until asynchronous execution completes.

+# Shapes, strides, broadcasting, and data types
+
+Correct graph construction requires both a logical view and an exact storage description.
+
+## Shapes and strides
+
+`dim[i]` is the extent of logical axis `i`. `stride[i]` is the distance in elements between adjacent indices on that axis. Contiguous row-major `[d0,d1,d2]` uses `[d1*d2,d2,1]`. Channels-last, transposed, sliced, and broadcast layouts use different strides without renaming logical axes.
+
+Alignment, vector count, vector dimension, and reorder type can further constrain which engines accept storage. A zero or overlapping stride is legal only where the individual API and engine permit it.
+
+## Broadcasting
+
+Pointwise Python IR aligns shapes from the right. Equal extents are compatible; an extent of `1` broadcasts. Matmul broadcasts leading batch dimensions but treats its final two dimensions as matrix axes. Operation-specific broadcasting can be narrower than general framework rules.
+
+## Data types
+
+IO data type defaults external tensors. Intermediate data type defaults virtual values. Compute data type controls accumulation or arithmetic. An operation-level compute type overrides the graph default, and an output tensor's data type still controls storage.
+
+Low-precision formats add scale layouts, block sizes, amax, reordering, and architecture constraints. Boolean, integer index, and pass-by-value tensors have operation-specific conversion rules.
+
+## Ragged and packed layouts
+
+Ragged offsets describe variable sequence starts, optionally multiplied by an element unit. THD attention packs tokens from several sequences. Block masks, page tables, and block scales use packed representations whose integer entries or bytes must be interpreted by the owning API, not by generic shape rules.

+# Numerical precision and block scaling
+
+Storage precision, compute precision, scaling, and output conversion are separate decisions.
+
+## Conventional floating point
+
+FP16 and BF16 commonly use FP32 accumulation. The output can remain FP32 or convert to an IO type. Reduction order and fused implementation can still produce small differences from a framework reference.
+
+## FP8
+
+FP8 extends range or precision through a scale. Operations may consume descale tensors and produce amax values used to update later scales. Hopper supports selected FP8 paths; individual APIs define layout and dimension constraints.
+
+## Block scaling
+
+MXFP8 and NVFP4 associate scales with fixed-size blocks rather than whole tensors. Scale layout, exponent representation, block axis, reorder type, and vectorization must match the consuming kernel. Blackwell provides the target architecture for these paths in the current checkout.
+
+## Error model
+
+Quantization can saturate large values, underflow small values, and add block-dependent relative error. Validate scale computation, amax, quantized distribution, dequantized values, operation output, and task-level quality.
+
+## Compatibility
+
+Never infer support from a data-type enum alone. A format can exist in the API while a particular operation, shape, architecture, or backend plan remains unsupported.

+# Operations and training dataflow
+
+Operation families differ in what forward must preserve for backward and which state crosses iteration boundaries.
+
+## Forward and backward pairs
+
+Convolution has forward, data-gradient, and weight-gradient operations. Pointwise activations often have a backward form that consumes the upstream gradient and either the forward input or output. RoPE backward uses the same frequency convention. SDPA backward needs the forward inputs, output, upstream gradient, and softmax statistics.
+
+## Saved statistics
+
+LayerNorm, BatchNorm, InstanceNorm, RMSNorm, and SDPA can emit statistics used later by backward. Keep them virtual only when backward is in the same graph. Materialize them when another graph or iteration consumes them.
+
+## Running state
+
+BatchNorm training can update running mean and variance. These are application state: bind current values, capture the next values, and define the update order. Do not confuse saved per-batch statistics with long-lived running state.
+
+## Auxiliary outputs
+
+Pooling indices, RNG dumps, amax values, scale tensors, routing metadata, and page-table state may be necessary for backward or the next operation. Their type, shape, and lifetime are part of the operation contract even when they are not the primary result.
+
+## Gradient verification
+
+Verify forward first, then each gradient independently. Match compute and output types, masks, layouts, epsilon, dropout state, and reduction axes. Use finite differences only where dtype and scale make them meaningful.

+# OSS engines and stability
+
+The repository combines cuDNN backend plans, Python execution engines, and open-source CUTLASS DSL kernels. They share graph goals but not identical packaging or compatibility promises.
+
+## Built-in backend
+
+The cuDNN backend is selected through heuristics and Graph plans. Its support surface depends on the installed backend, GPU, graph metadata, and plan policy.
+
+## Python engines
+
+`BaseEngine`, `PlanConfig`, `ExecutionContext`, the static engine manifest, and family heuristic hooks define an unreleased in-tree extension path. Engines own exact support checks, compilation, workspace reporting, and execution on caller context. Applications cannot register engines at runtime.
+
+## OSS packages
+
+Optional packages export fused SDPA, sparse attention, normalization, dense/grouped GEMM, and projection/RoPE kernels. They require the `cutedsl` dependency set and have explicit architecture, layout, shape, and dtype ranges. Package `__all__` is the public boundary; implementation modules are not automatically public.
+
+## Experimental operators
+
+`cudnn.experimental.ops` exposes PyTorch-facing functions that can change more quickly. An experimental label must appear in its reference page, local compatibility constraints, import path, and sample catalog entry.
+
+## Fallback
+
+Graph OSS heuristic selection can retain backend candidates. Direct package wrappers may not fall back. Applications should treat unsupported signals differently from programming or execution errors.

+# Python IR routing invariants
+
+`cudnn.pygraph` stores an inspectable Python operation DAG, then ranks the in-tree Python engines for that graph family together with cuDNN backend plans. These invariants keep routing deterministic and prevent a plan from observing a graph different from the graph it accepted.
+
+## Operation declaration mechanisms
+
+The Python IR covers the public Graph operation surface through three source-owned registries plus explicit methods:
+
+- `_POINTWISE_TENSOR_ARGS` installs uniform pointwise builders whose mode matches the method name.
+- `_STRUCTURED_OPS` describes named input ports, scalar attributes, outputs, and shape inference for convolution, normalization, reduction, block scaling, MoE, and structural operations.
+- `_CAPTURED_OPS` records explicit schemas for SDPA variants with many conditional inputs and outputs.
+- `matmul` remains explicit because its positional calling convention is independently useful.
+
+Input and output port names match the C++ binding keyword names. An engine should inspect `NodeType`, named ports, parameter values, tensor metadata, and graph context instead of depending on insertion order.
+
+## Engine contract
+
+A `BaseEngine` checks support and builds a `PlanConfig` selected by family heuristics. Building a plan performs expensive specialization once. A compiled plan executes with caller-provided tensor data and an `ExecutionContext` containing handle, stream, workspace, and dynamic overrides.
+
+`python/cudnn/engines/manifest.py` is the only engine registry. Applications cannot add engines at runtime. Each family owns a fixed engine-ID block, and slots must remain stable for reproducible selection and cache identity. An engine declines only with one of the documented decline exception types. Any other exception is an implementation defect and propagates rather than silently trying another engine.
+
+## Routed and backend plan spaces
+
+The routed list contains eligible in-tree Python plans and cuDNN backend entries. `select_plan()` addresses this combined list. A backend entry may refer to a specific backend-plan index or delegate to backend heuristics when the backend does not expose its candidates. A routed index must never be interpreted as a backend plan index.
+
+Family heuristic hooks may return only engine IDs owned by that family. A `BACKEND` marker places the backend block relative to Python candidates; the common assembler expands the marker, combines heuristic-mode blocks, and removes duplicate `(engine_id, knobs)` entries.
+
+## UID ownership
+
+The Python IR owns the graph UID namespace. User-assigned UIDs are pushed explicitly when creating the backend graph representation. Two user-assigned tensors cannot share a UID. When a user UID collides with an automatically assigned UID, the automatically assigned tensor is renumbered so the explicit user contract wins.
+
+Bind each required non-virtual UID exactly once at execution. UID equality does not establish shape, stride, dtype, device, or lifetime compatibility.
+
+## Pure execution paths
+
+A graph selected for a Python engine executes without creating a C++ backend graph representation. A graph selected for the backend creates that representation from the complete Python IR and delegates planning and execution. Mixed construction, where some nodes are built directly in C++ and others in the Python IR, is unsupported.
+
+Explicitly querying backend plan methods requests backend graph creation even when Python engines are available. Applications should not use those methods merely to inspect a Python-engine plan.
+
+## One-shot planning and freeze
+
+`create_execution_plans()` is one-shot. Use `select_plan()` to switch among already proposed entries; construct a new graph to run routing with different policy.
+
+Creating the graph representation or planning freezes the graph's entire public mutation surface: graph operation builders, fluent tensor and node setters, direct metadata assignment, node input/output/parameter mappings, and in-place dimension or stride edits. Inspection remains available. A mutation after validation but before freeze invalidates validation and requires validation again.
+
+## Output layout ownership
+
+Only output dimensions and strides explicitly assigned by the user are authoritative when creating the graph representation. Python-inferred strides are provisional. When no explicit layout is supplied, the cuDNN backend retains operation-specific inference, such as preserving a convolution layout family.
+
+An engine that requires a concrete output layout must either accept the user-assigned layout or establish its own documented output contract during support checking. It must not assume every provisional Python row-major stride was a user requirement.
+
+## Prove the selected path
+
+Backend-path tests should check numerics and dispatch state: `graph.selected_engine` is `None`, backend plans exist, and a backend graph representation was created. Python-engine tests should assert the selected manifest engine and verify that unsupported graphs are rejected. Do not assert backend kernel names because those names are internal and version-dependent.
+
+Current sources: [Python graph implementation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/0a07d4ee28f8ae2f2106bb766b1878cc732ee80c/python/cudnn/_pygraph.py#L44) and [engine contract](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/0a07d4ee28f8ae2f2106bb766b1878cc732ee80c/python/cudnn/engines/base.py#L1).
+
+## Availability
+
+Python IR routing is unreleased behavior in this checkout. Manifest slots,
+family heuristics, UID collision handling, freeze boundaries, plan
+compatibility, and pure-Python execution contracts can change before release.

+# Runtime resources and asynchronous execution
+
+Graph construction describes reusable computation. Execution supplies context and storage for one invocation.
+
+## Handles and streams
+
+A cuDNN handle selects a CUDA stream and carries backend context. Changing its stream affects subsequent work. The high-level Python wrapper binds its managed handle to PyTorch's current stream; explicit APIs use caller-supplied handles.
+
+## Variant packs
+
+A variant pack maps every required non-virtual UID to a device pointer and includes workspace. Tensor descriptors do not own those buffers. Pass-by-value and ragged-offset values can add bindings beyond obvious inputs and outputs.
+
+## Workspace
+
+Workspace is temporary storage sized for a built plan. It can be reused after prior asynchronous work completes. Concurrent executions need independent storage unless the plan contract explicitly permits sharing.
+
+## Lifetime and synchronization
+
+Execution normally enqueues work and returns before completion. Keep graph, plan, handle, input, output, scalar, auxiliary, and workspace resources alive until the stream reaches the operation. Synchronize only for host access, timing, error localization, or dependency not already expressed by streams and events.
+
+## CUDA Graph interaction
+
+CUDA Graph capture adds stronger address and lifetime requirements. Resources captured by address must remain stable across replay; unsupported changes require repopulation.

+def setup_context(ctx, inputs, output) -> None:
+    del output
+    ctx.save_for_backward(*inputs)
+
+
+def backward(ctx, grad_output: torch.Tensor):
+    a, b = ctx.saved_tensors
+    grad_a = (grad_output @ b.transpose(-2, -1)).sum_to_size(a.shape)
+    grad_b = (a.transpose(-2, -1) @ grad_output).sum_to_size(b.shape)
+    return grad_a, grad_b
+

+def tensor_key(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> TensorKey:
+    return str(tensor.device), tensor.dtype, tuple(tensor.shape), tuple(tensor.stride())

+        compute_data_type=torch.float32,
+        inputs=["matmul::A", "matmul::B"],
+        outputs=["C"],
+        handle="auto",
+    ) as graph:
+        output = graph.matmul(name="matmul", A=a, B=b)

+
+
+def cached_matmul(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    key = graph_key(a, b)
+    graph = GRAPH_CACHE.get(key)
+    if graph is None:
+        graph = build_graph(a, b)
+        GRAPH_CACHE[key] = graph
+    return graph(a, b)
+```

+# Choose an interface
+
+There are multiple interfaces to choose from to integrate cuDNN into your application.
+Choose the interface that exposes the control your application actually needs.
+
+| Interface | Lifecycle ownership | Runtime buffers | Use it when |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `cudnn.Graph` (Python) | Automatic at context exit | PyTorch inputs; wrapper allocates outputs/workspace | Building Python or PyTorch applications quickly |
+| `cudnn.pygraph` (Python) | Explicit or `build()` convenience | Caller binds tensors/workspace | Inspecting IR, routing engines, filtering plans, or serializing |
+| `graph::Graph` (C++) | Explicit | Caller owns handle, pointers, workspace, synchronization | Integrating into C++ services or runtimes |
+| `cudnn.graph` / `cudnn.jit` (Python) | Automatic and cached | PyTorch | Shape-specialized decorated Python functions |
+| `cudnn.ops` (Python) | PyTorch dispatcher owns schema/autograd | PyTorch | Using a supplied convenience operator such as causal Conv1d |
+| OSS packages (Python) | Package-specific | Usually PyTorch/CUTLASS DSL tensors | Using an exact architecture-specific fused kernel |
+| `cudnn.experimental.ops` (Python) | PyTorch convenience wrapper | PyTorch | Evaluating explicitly experimental features |
+| Legacy C++ builders | Explicit descriptors | Caller owned | Maintaining existing code while migrating |
+
+Start with `cudnn.Graph` for Python learning. Move to `cudnn.pygraph` when you can name the lifecycle or routing control you need. Start C++ directly when the host application is C++ or must own every resource.
+
+Python IR and engine routing are unreleased in this checkout. See the
+[routing availability and invariants](/concepts/python-ir-routing#availability)
+before depending on that interface.
+
+Optional wrappers can be faster or more specialized, but their layouts, dependencies, architecture range, stability, and fallback behavior are narrower. Evaluate them through [Select OSS engines and kernels](/optional-kernels/oss-engines).

+# Installation
+
+Using cuDNN Frontend requires a compatible CUDA, cuDNN, driver, and GPU stack. Depends on whether you want to use Python or C++ interface, you can setup the environment differently.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Python 3.10 or newer for the Python package.
+- CMake 3.26 or newer and a C++17 compiler for repository CMake builds.
+- An NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit/runtime, and cuDNN release that support the selected feature.
+- Linux or Windows for the core package. Optional CUTLASS DSL packages can have narrower platform support.
+
+<Tabs>
+<Tab title="Python" language="python">
+
+
+## Python
+
+Install the released package from PyPI:
+
+```bash
+pip install nvidia-cudnn-frontend
+```
+
+The base package includes the graph API and the framework-neutral CuTeDSL
+dependencies on supported platforms. The compatibility extra
+`nvidia-cudnn-frontend[cutedsl]` still resolves, but currently adds only
+`cuda-python`. Install a CUDA-enabled PyTorch or JAX build separately when an
+API uses that framework.
+
+To install from source, clone the repository and run:
+
+```bash
+# optional: Set the paths if CUDA or cuDNN are not in default system locations
+export CUDAToolkit_ROOT=/path/to/cuda
+export CUDA_PATH=/path/to/cuda
+export CUDNN_PATH=/path/to/cudnn
+
+# Install the graph API and framework-neutral CuTeDSL dependencies
+pip install -e .
+
+# Optional: Add a tensor framework for framework-specific CuTeDSL APIs
+pip install --group torch
+# or: pip install --group jax
+```
+
+The source build uses CMake and nanobind to build `cudnn._compiled_module`.
+Set `CUDAToolkit_ROOT` or `CUDA_PATH` when CMake cannot find the intended
+toolkit. Set `CUDNN_PATH` when cuDNN headers or libraries are outside normal
+discovery paths.
+
+## Verify the installation
+
+After activating the Python environment you want to test, run the probe from
+the repository root:
+
+```bash
+python docs/samples/python/verify_environment.py
+```
+
+The path printed as `cudnn_file` must resolve under this checkout when testing
+unreleased source behavior. A site-packages path tests the installed wheel.
+
+</Tab>
+<Tab title="C++" language="cpp">
+
+
+## C++
+
+The C++ frontend is header-only. The header files are located at `include/` directory. The main header file is `cudnn_frontend.h`. Applications still need to link cuDNN and the CUDA libraries they call. You can find instructions on how to install cuDNN and CUDA libraries from the following links:
+
+- CUDA: [https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-downloads)
+- cuDNN: [https://developer.nvidia.com/cudnn-downloads](https://developer.nvidia.com/cudnn-downloads)
+
+You can add this repository as a CMake subdirectory and link `cudnn_frontend` with appropriate libraries. Below is an example of the `CMakeLists.txt` to use the cuDNN Frontend:
+
+<Code
+  src="../samples/cmake/CMakeLists.txt"
+  language="cmake"
+  maxLines={0}
+/>
+
+Configure a source-tree build with samples and tests disabled when only the package target is needed:
+
+```bash
+cmake -S . -B build/install \
+  -DCUDNN_FRONTEND_BUILD_SAMPLES=OFF \
+  -DCUDNN_FRONTEND_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
+  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/path/to/prefix
+cmake --build build/install
+cmake --install build/install
+```
+
+Then set `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/prefix` for the consuming project. On Windows, use the appropriate MSVC generator and ensure cuDNN/CUDA DLL directories are on `PATH`. On Linux, ensure shared libraries are discoverable through the dynamic loader or package installation.
+
+</Tab>
+</Tabs>
+## Optional: Select the CUDA runtime
+
+When several `libcudart.so` major versions are visible, in your system, you may need to set the exact runtime required by the environment before running any cuDNN application. This applies to both Python and C++ interfaces:
+
+```bash
+export CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME=libcudart.so.13
+```
+
+Do not set that value automatically on a CUDA 12 deployment. Record the chosen library with test results.
+
+## Next steps
+
+Run the [Python and C++ quick starts](/getting-started/quickstart) to learn how to use the cuDNN Frontend and verify your installation.
+
+## Verification limits
+
+The repository README states cuDNN 8.5 as a general frontend minimum, while the
+Python `cudnn.Graph` wrapper requires backend 9.12. Treat minimum versions as
+interface-specific. Windows installation is source-supported but was not
+executed in the recorded verification environment.

+# Quick start
+
+Below is a quick start example that builds and executes a batched BF16 matrix multiplication using cuDNN. Tensor `A` has shape `[2, 4, 8]`, tensor `B` has shape `[1, 8, 6]`, and cuDNN broadcasts `B` across the batch dimension to produce `C` with shape `[2, 4, 6]`.
+
+The Python and C++ examples implement the same graph. Python uses the high-level `cudnn.Graph` wrapper to manage the graph lifecycle. C++ exposes each lifecycle operation so that resource ownership and runtime bindings are explicit.
+
+The Python `cudnn.Graph` wrapper requires cuDNN backend 9.12 or newer; the
+repository's general frontend minimum of 8.5 does not apply to this wrapper.
+
+<Tabs>
+<Tab title="Python" language="python">
+
+
+The Python wrapper accepts PyTorch CUDA tensors while the graph is being described. It records their metadata and later accepts the actual runtime buffers through a function-like call.
+
+<Code
+  src="../samples/python/matmul.py"
+  language="python"
+  maxLines={0}
+/>
+
+Run the sample from the repository root:
+
+<Markdown src="/snippets/generated/shell/run_quickstarts/python.mdx" />
+
+The example performs these steps:
+
+1. **Allocate runtime inputs.** `a_data` and `b_data` are BF16 PyTorch tensors on the GPU. Their shapes define a batched matmul, and the singleton leading dimension of `b_data` makes it broadcast across both batches of `a_data`. The random values are runtime data, but their shapes, strides, and dtypes also provide the metadata needed to describe the graph.
+
+2. **Open a `cudnn.Graph` construction context.** `io_data_type` sets the default type of values entering and leaving the graph. `compute_data_type=torch.float32` requests FP32 matmul accumulation, which is more accurate than BF16 accumulation. `inputs` and `outputs` define the positional call contract: the first argument to `graph(...)` binds to `matmul::A`, the second binds to `matmul::B`, and the tensor named `C` is returned. `handle="auto"` makes the wrapper reuse a default cuDNN handle and bind it to PyTorch's current CUDA stream at execution time. Note that in this example, the data type of the input tensors are inferred from the PyTorch tensors and that of the output tensor is set explicitly. Hence setting `io_data_type` is redundant.
+
+3. **Add the matmul operation.** `graph.matmul(...)` captures the PyTorch tensors through their DLPack-compatible interface and creates cuDNN tensor descriptors from their metadata. It does not consume any tensor values while constructing the graph. Naming the node `matmul` gives its inputs the stable canonical names `matmul::A` and `matmul::B` used by the graph's input list.
+
+4. **Declare the external output.** `set_output(True)` makes the result non-virtual, so cuDNN writes it to caller-visible storage instead of treating it as an internal temporary. `set_name("C")` connects the descriptor to `outputs=["C"]`, and `set_data_type(torch.bfloat16)` requests a BF16 result after FP32 accumulation.
+
+5. **Build the graph when the context closes.** Exiting the `with` block validates the graph, builds the backend operation graph, creates execution plans from the default heuristic modes, checks hardware support, builds the viable plans, and allocates workspace for the selected plan. This host-side preparation is intended to happen once for a compatible set of tensor metadata.
+
+6. **Execute with runtime buffers.** `graph(a_data, b_data)` maps the positional arguments to the declared inputs, allocates a PyTorch output tensor with the inferred shape and stride, supplies the wrapper-managed workspace, and enqueues the selected plan on PyTorch's current CUDA stream. Because there is one declared output, the call returns one tensor rather than a tuple.
+
+7. **Verify the result.** The PyTorch reference converts the inputs to FP32 before multiplication to match cuDNN's requested compute type, then converts the result to BF16 to match `C`. `torch.testing.assert_close` checks the complete result using tolerances appropriate for BF16 output.
+
+Keep `graph` alive and call it repeatedly to amortize graph construction overhead. Rebuild it when the input shape, stride, dtype, operation attributes, or other graph metadata changes.
+
+</Tab>
+<Tab title="C++" language="cpp">
+
+
+The C++ frontend describes the same operation as the Python counterpart, but the application creates the cuDNN handle, allocates output and workspace storage, binds device pointers, checks status values, and releases resources itself.
+
+<Code
+  src="../samples/cpp/matmul.cc"
+  language="cpp"
+  maxLines={0}
+/>
+
+Compile and run from the repository root:
+
+<Markdown src="/snippets/generated/shell/run_quickstarts/cpp.mdx" />
+
+The example performs these steps:
+
+1. **Fix the problem dimensions.** The constants describe `A[batch, m, k]`, `B[1, k, n]`, and `C[batch, m, n]`. `B` has one batch and is broadcast across `A`; the inner `k` dimensions match, which is required by matrix multiplication.
+
+2. **Allocate unified storage.** `cudaMallocManaged` reserves buffers for both BF16 inputs and the FP32 output. Managed allocations have one address that is accessible from the CPU and GPU, so this first example does not need separate host vectors or explicit host-to-device copies. CUDA migrates or maps the memory as each processor accesses it, and the application remains responsible for releasing it with `cudaFree`.
+
+3. **Initialize deterministic inputs.** The host writes `1` to `A` and `2` to `B` through their managed pointers. Each output is therefore the sum of eight products `1 * 2`, making `16` an exact, easy-to-check expected value. These allocations belong to the application; graph tensor objects created later only describe how cuDNN interprets their memory.
+
+4. **Create a cuDNN handle.** The handle carries the cuDNN execution context, including the CUDA stream on which work is enqueued. This sample uses the handle's default stream. An application with its own stream should call `cudnnSetStream` before building or executing the graph.
+
+5. **Set graph-wide data types.** `set_io_data_type(BFLOAT16)` establishes the default external type. FP32 intermediate and compute types request higher-precision accumulation. Individual tensor descriptors can override these defaults, as the output does.
+
+6. **Describe tensor layouts.** Each `Tensor_attributes` object supplies a name, dimensions, row-major strides, and data type. For example, `A` uses strides `{m * k, k, 1}`, so advancing its batch, row, or column index moves the expected number of elements. `B` uses a leading dimension of one, which expresses batch broadcasting.
+
+7. **Add the operation and expose its result.** `graph.matmul(a, b, ...)` adds a matmul node and returns its output descriptor. `set_output(true)` tells cuDNN that `C` requires application-provided storage. Setting `C` to FP32 keeps the accumulated result in FP32 rather than converting it back to BF16.
+
+8. **Build a reusable execution plan.** `graph.build(...)` validates the graph, queries the `A` and `FALLBACK` heuristic modes for candidate engine configurations, checks whether they are supported by the current cuDNN backend and GPU, and builds a plan. A failed status includes the diagnostic returned by the frontend.
+
+9. **Allocate plan workspace.** `get_workspace_size()` reports temporary GPU memory required by the selected plan. The application allocates it only when the size is nonzero and can reuse that allocation across executions of this graph.
+
+10. **Create the variant pack.** The map binds each graph tensor descriptor to its runtime device pointer. This separates the reusable graph and plan from a particular set of input and output buffers; a later execution can supply different pointers with compatible layouts and types.
+
+11. **Execute the plan.** `graph.execute(...)` enqueues work using the handle, variant pack, and workspace. Because execution is asynchronous with respect to the host, the example calls `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` before the CPU reads the managed output buffer.
+
+12. **Validate and release resources.** After synchronization, the loop reads `c_dev` directly from the host and checks every output against `16.0f`. Small C++17 RAII owners call `cudaFree` for workspace and managed tensors and call `cudnnDestroy` for the handle on both success and early error returns. The application still owns those resources; RAII only makes that ownership exception-safe.
+
+As in Python, build once and execute repeatedly while tensor metadata and operation attributes remain compatible. Rebind the variant pack when only the device addresses change.
+
+</Tab>
+</Tabs>
+Graph construction runs on the host. Execution consumes the device pointers supplied for non-virtual inputs and outputs. Reuse the built graph when shapes, strides, data types, and supported dynamic-shape overrides remain compatible.

+# Configure attention recipes
+
+Add one attention feature at a time to a verified dense SDPA baseline. Every recipe changes the support surface and cache key.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Complete the [attention tutorial](/tutorials/attention) and keep its dense
+forward and backward checks as a baseline. Confirm the version, architecture,
+dtype, layout, and backward support of every feature you add.
+
+## Training and inference
+
+Set `generate_stats=True` for a forward result that will feed `sdpa_backward`. Inference can omit statistics. Keep forward output and statistics alive until backward completes.
+
+## Masks
+
+- Diagonal bands express causal and sliding-window limits with explicit top-left or bottom-right alignment.
+- Padding masks require query and key/value sequence-length tensors.
+- Block masks use a packed tile representation and require an implementation that supports them. On SM10x, they require cuDNN 9.26 or newer.
+- A score modifier function inserts a graph callback before softmax and cannot be combined with every built-in mask path.
+
+## Layouts and state
+
+Dense BSHD/BHSD layouts use explicit strides. THD packs variable sequences and uses ragged offsets. Paged attention treats K/V as cache containers and uses integer page tables plus a logical maximum sequence length. Sink tokens add persistent score state.
+
+## Dropout
+
+Use either probability plus Philox seed/offset tensors, or an explicit mask plus scale. The mask applies after softmax. Preserve seed/offset progression across executions and expose RNG dump only when needed for backward or diagnostics.
+
+## Low precision
+
+FP8 and MXFP8 paths add descale, scale, amax, reorder, dimension, and architecture constraints. Validate against a higher-precision baseline before tuning.
+
+Published recipes: [causal BF16](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/main/docs/samples/python/sdpa_bf16_causal.py), [dropout](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/main/docs/samples/python/sdpa_dropout.py), [paged KV cache](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/main/docs/samples/python/sdpa_paged_kv_cache.py), [C++ block mask](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/main/docs/samples/cpp/sdpa_block_mask.cc), and [sliding window](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/main/docs/samples/python/sdpa_sliding_window_chunked_prefill.py).
+
+## Expected result
+
+Each linked sample executes one focused variation. Your derived graph should
+continue to match the dense baseline wherever the feature is inactive and
+should fail during support checking, rather than execution, when the selected
+backend cannot implement the requested combination.
